text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov handed a mandate to the ruling Socialist Party to form a new government.

The Socialists' nominee for premier Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev said the party would accept the mandate despite the presidential appeal that Socialists refuse the mandate and agree to the opposition demands for early elections. @

-- Oposition leaders said after a meeting with the president the opposition would return to parliament to vote on urgently needed economic reform bills only if the Socialists give up their mandate to form a new cabinet.
-- Leaders of the Socialist party and its parliamentary allies decided to insist on forming a programme cabinet of non-party technocrats to get the country out of the economic crisis. @

-- British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, who was on a one-day visit to Sofia, appealed to President Petar Stoyanov to unravel the so-called "umbrella murder" of Bulgaria's dissident Georgi Markov in London 19 years ago.
-- Mass street protests were held on Tuesday in Sofia for 23rd consecutive day against forming a second cabinet by the ruling Socialists and for immediate general elections.
-- Bulgaria's three main trade unions called a nationwide general strike on Wednesday demanding immediate general elections and against forming a new cabinet by the Socialists.
-- Bulgaria transferred $135.1 million to Brady Bond coupon payment to debt agent Citibank of Citicorp which distributes the payment to investors, deputy finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said.

-- Bulgaria's national carrier Balkan Airlines will be restructured in a move to stabilise finances and return to profit before its planned privatisation, Balkan's executive director Valeri Doganov said.
